title: Insights from Rights and Wrongs: A Large Language Model for Solving Assertion Failures in RTL Design
problem: Assertion failures in SystemVerilog RTL designs require manual analysis of complex logical and timing relationships between signals to identify and fix the underlying issues. No automated tool currently assists engineers in solving these failures.
motivation: Debugging assertion failures is a labor-intensive task requiring deep expertise in RTL design, and automating this process would significantly accelerate hardware design verification.
method: AssertSolver trains an AI language model on synthetic data—artificially created examples from challenging hardware test cases—teaching it to recognize assertion failures (automated checks that verify designs work correctly). The model strengthens itself by learning from its own mistakes through error feedback. When given a failing assertion and its corresponding RTL code (the detailed hardware logic), it predicts the needed bug fix, achieving an 88.54% success rate on the first attempt.
key_novelty: AssertSolver is an AI language model trained specifically for fixing hardware assertion failures using artificially created test cases and learning from its own mistakes.
contributions: Specialized LLM trained for RTL assertion failure diagnosis and bug fixing
Public testbench and model release for reproducibility
88.54% pass@1 bug-fixing accuracy, 11.97% improvement over o1-preview
Demonstration of LLM efficacy for hardware verification automation
limitations: Paper focuses on assertion failure solving; generalization to other RTL verification tasks not discussed.
primary_theme: LLM for automated RTL assertion debugging
